note: OpenZeppelin smart-account builds whose rules a review will read. The review `revoke_policy` returns for the rule it removes reads an account's rules only when it runs one of these builds: an account that runs other code could answer with any rule. packages/policy-synth/src/config.ts lists the same hashes (OZ_ACCOUNT_WASM); config.test.ts holds the two together. Two builds are trusted side by side: the 0.7.2-line account every existing Prime and mainnet account runs (the seat 393f0e5d is tied to its digest), and OpenZeppelin's v0.8.0 account, which the testnet reference account runs.

sources.multisig_account_example: contracts/stellar/policy-interpreter/tests/fixtures/multisig_account_example.wasm (sha256 as listed, committed as a blob so the suite pins the deployed bytes); the live-test account CASJ5GECFWVHCOJHFPE3TJKHLZNBUYNBJ4UAK6JRWHU2HEL3WFGMGM5P runs it, and so does every Prime the app deploys
sources.multisig_account_example_v0_8_0: contracts/stellar/policy-interpreter/tests/fixtures/oz_0_8_0_multisig_account_example.wasm (sha256 as listed); the testnet reference account CDS2W673EV22FDZX7FB6PDSTPJ7MMPONVXAGITNC2ABBVJ65TGA2ACUL runs it

multisig_account_example.whatIsKnown: The bytes are the blob above, and the live testnet account runs the same hash. The upstream commit and the build command that produced the blob are NOT recorded anywhere in this repository. The round-9 design record (contracts/prime/ARCHITECTURE.md, kept at tag archive/spike-final) cites OpenZeppelin stellar-contracts at ce5c568 for how account calls are authorised; that is a documentation reference, not a build record (ce5c568 is v0.8.0-rc.3 plus 76 commits, dated 2026-10-07, after the account code was deployed).

reproductionAttempts.source: OpenZeppelin/stellar-contracts release-v0.7.2 (a9c4216, the tag the deployed policies were built from, evidence/README.md)

multisig_account_example.consequence: The hash is a pin on the deployed bytes, not a claim that they reproduce from a named source. Treat a review of an account on this build as trusting the OpenZeppelin account's `get_context_rule` answers, as the install path already does.
